summary: U.S.-founded digital-asset platform whose retail Abra Earn and accredited-investor Abra Boost interest accounts lent customer crypto through institutional and DeFi strategies before the U.S. yield products were wound down amid state and federal regulatory actions; Abra continues as a private-client and institutional business.
what_happened: Abra began offering Abra Earn to U.S. retail investors around July 2020. Customer crypto was placed through a third-party custodian and deployed under Abra's direction through institutional lending, DeFi lending, and other revenue-generating strategies. Abra stopped selling new Abra Earn accounts around 3 October 2022 and briefly offered Abra Boost to accredited investors. On 14 June 2023, Abra converted Earn and Boost balances into non-interest-bearing Abra Trade accounts, stopped generating yield, and asked U.S. customers to withdraw. State settlements established procedures for returning remaining assets, and the SEC filed settled registration charges in August 2024. The former U.S. retail Earn business is closed, while the Abra brand remains active for private and institutional clients.
uncertainty_notes: The July 2020 launch date uses the first day of the month as a sortable approximation because the SEC states only that Abra Earn began around July 2020. Abra itself remains active, so the platform is classified as limited rather than operations_ended; the closure applies to the historical U.S. retail Earn and Boost products.
notes: Added as a non-insolvency regulatory wind-down case. Final completion of every remaining customer-asset return was not independently established, so the outcome is not classified as full repayment.
